items.title: The determinant of a perfect complex of tor amplitude in two degrees is a functor to invertible modules, with a canonical element carrying isomorphisms
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma packages the determinant constructions of the surrounding section into a functor det from the category of perfect complexes with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] and isomorphisms as morphisms, to the category of invertible modules with isomorphisms as morphisms; it also asserts that a rank 0 perfect object L with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] carries a canonical element delta(L) in det(L) such that for every isomorphism a : L -> K in D(R) one has det(a)(delta(L)) = delta(K) (source lines 37123-37147). The proof is a substantial construction-and-verification. It first calls a two-term complex with finite projective terms good, notes that every object of the source category is represented by one, and that morphisms between good complexes in the derived category are homotopy classes of maps of complexes, so that the previously studied determinant det(L^bullet) = det(L^0) tensor det(L^{-1})^{tensor -1} can be used (proof lines 37150-37162). For a quasi-isomorphism a^bullet : L^bullet -> K^bullet it introduces the notion of a good diagram: a commuting-up-to-homotopy triangle through an auxiliary good complex M^bullet whose maps b^bullet and c^bullet satisfy the three conditions established earlier; det(a^bullet) is then defined as det(c^bullet) composed with det(b^bullet)^{-1}, and the proof must show that good diagrams always exist and that this definition does not depend on the diagram chosen (proof lines 37165-37182). Existence is constructive: choosing a surjection R^{oplus n} -> K^{-1}, the proof builds the good complex M^bullet = (L^{-1} oplus R^{oplus n}) -> (L^0 oplus R^{oplus n}) with the projection b^bullet and the map c^bullet using a^{-1} oplus p in degree -1 and a^0 oplus d o p in degree 0, and checks the conditions (proof lines 37185-37200). Independence for the identity is then immediate from the homotopic-surjections lemma, which gives det(c^bullet) = det(b^bullet) for a good diagram over the identity, so det(id^bullet) = id (proof lines 37203-37213). The proof continues by analysing composition of quasi-isomorphisms and good diagrams, and completes the independence, functoriality and the canonical element delta by the same diagrammatic machinery (rest of the counted proof span, source lines 37216-37290). The non-routine content is the existence construction for good diagrams, the use of the homotopic-surjections lemma to get independence over the identity, and the diagrammatic treatment of composition.
